newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA RUPEE ENDS FLAT ON HIGH DLR SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA RUPEE ENDS FLAT ON HIGH DLR SUPPLY.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed barely moved against the dollar on Wednesday despite imports as the market was well supplied with the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.91 to the dollar after opening at 58.92, they said.
"The exchange rate was steady due to the market being well supplied with dollars and not because there was a lack of commercial demand," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Dealers said the inflow of dollars into Sri Lanka has been high in recent months due to increased foreign participation in the Colombo stock market and privatisations.
Overnight call money closed at its opening level of 12 percent, after rising to 13.5, dealers said.
"Money rates should fall soon because many banks are selling dollars to the central bank," said one.
The central bank pushed up the dollar by half a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.9149 and 60.1051.
